A rectangular plate of dimensions 150 mm × 300 mm is subjected to four forces acting at various
points as shown in the figure. Determine magnitude and direction of the resultant force and its
location from edge C of the plate.
Determine the reactions at all the supports of the beam shown in the figure below.
Determine the centroid for the shaded portion shown in the figure w.r.t axes shown.

For the plane area shown in the figure, determine the moment of inertia and the radius of gyration
about the OX-axis.

A tapered bar of rectangular cross section is 40 mm wide at one end and 75 mm wide at the other,
10 mm thick and 1 m long. The elongation of 0.1 mm was observed under load P. Determine the
load P, if the modulus of elasticity of the material of the bar is 100 GPa. Also calculate stress at 600
mm from point A.

A composite prismatic bar consists of three sections rigidly fastened in series as shown in the figure
below. Determine the stress in each section, change in length of each section and total change in
length of the bar.

A circular rod of 30 mm diameter and 550 mm long is subjected to a tensile force of 70 kN.
Determine modulus of rigidity, bulk modulus and change in volume if Poisson's ratio = 0.3 and
Young's modulus E = 2 × 105 N/mm2.

A thin cylindrical shell is 4m long and 1m in internal diameter. It is subjected to an internal pressure
of 1.4 MPa. If the thickness of the sheet is 14mm, determine the circumferential stress, longitudinal
stress, changes in diameter, length and volume. Take E=200 GPa and µ= 0.3.

A steel rod of 30 mm diameter is enclosed centrally in a hollow copper tube of external diameter 50
mm and internal diameter of 40 mm. The composite bar is then subjected to an axial pull of 45 kN.
If the length of each bar is equal to 150 mm, determine: (i)The stresses in the rod and tube, and (ii)
The load carried by each bar. Take E for steel =2.1 × 105 N/mm2 and for copper =1.1×105 N/mm2.

A rod is composed of three segments, as shown in the figure. Compute the stress induced in each
material by a temperature drop 30 °C if (a) the walls are rigid and
(b) Both the supports yield by 0.3 mm.

A block A weighing 80 kN is to be moved towards left by light wedge B as shown in the figure
below. Determine the necessary force P required to move block A, if angle of friction at all rubbing
surfaces is 15°.
Determine the centroid for the shaded portion for the figure below w.r.t. X and Y axes.

For the shaded area shown in the figure, determine the moment of inertia and the radius of gyration
about the X-axis.

A solid circular bar of length L = 1.2 m tapers linearly from diameter d1 = 30 mm (large end) to d2 =
20 mm (small end). The bar is loaded in tension with an axial load P = 40 kN. The material has yield
strength 250 MPa and Young's modulus E = 200 GPa.
Determine:
i) The axial (working) stress at the large and small ends.
ii) The factor of safety against yielding based on the maximum stress.
The total change in length (elongation) of the tapered bar under the load.

A surgeon requires that the inner diameter at C be 10.0 mm for a medical purpose. The bone at C
will carry an axial tensile load of 1500 N and the allowable average normal stress (from the strain
gauge limit) is 3.20 MPa. The modulus of elasticity of the bone material is 18 GPa, and the effective
length of the loaded bone section is 200 mm. A factor of safety (F.S.) = 1.5 must also be considered
in the design. Determine the minimum outer diameter required at C (in mm) so that average stress
does not exceed the allowable and the elongation of the bone section under the applied load.

A bar of 25 mm diameter is tested in tension. It is observed that when a load of 60kN is applied, the
extension measured over a gauge length of 200 mm is 0.12 mm and the contraction in diameter is
0.0045 mm. Determine Poisson's ratio and elastic constants E, G, K.

A cylindrical shell 3m long, which is closed at the ends, has an internal diameter of 1.5m and a wall
thickness of 20mm. Determine the circumferential and longitudinal stresses induced, and the
change in the dimensions of the steel. If it is subjected to an internal pressure of 1.5 N/mm2.Take
E=2×105N/mm2 and Poisson's ratio=0.3

Three bars made of copper, zinc and aluminium are of equal length and have cross-sections 500,
750 and 1000 square mm, respectively. They are rigidly connected at their ends. If the compound
member is subjected to a longitudinal pull of 250 kN. Determine the proportion of the load carried by
each rod and the induced stresses. Take the value of E for copper = 1.3 × 105 N/mm2, for zinc = 1.0
× 105 N/mm2 and for aluminium = 0.8 × 105 N/mm2.

A composite bar is made by attaching a copper rod of length 900 mm and diameter 30 mm, and a
brass rod of length 600 mm and diameter 45 mm, as shown in Fig. A load of 20 kN is applied at
20°C. Determine the stresses in the materials when the temperature rises to 50°C. Take Ec = 120
GPa, αc= 18 x 10-6/°C, Eb = 90 GPa and αa= 20 x 10-6/ °C.

A steel rail is 12 m long and is laid at a temperature of 18°C. The maximum temperature expected
is 40°C.
(i) Estimate the minimum gap between two rails to be left so that the temperature stresses do not
develop.
(ii) Calculate the temperature stresses developed in the rails if:
(a) No expansion joint is provided.
(b) If a 1.5 mm gap is provided for expansion.
Take E = 2 × 105 N/mm2 and α = 12 × 10-6/°C.

considering Poisson's ratio=0.3 and E=100GPa.

strengthened by 4 steel bars at the corners with total c/s area of 4800 mm2. If Es=15Ec,
a) Determine the stress in steel and concrete.
